rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong baseline for the full multimodal pipeline. config_020 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) combines the most expressive choices across all dimensions: a learned biological latent (scvi_n200), a strong pretrained vision backbone (imagenet_vit_l), the most flexible aggregation (transformer), and a learned fusion (weighted). This tests the core hypothesis that multimodal fusion with rich representations outperforms simpler alternatives, and provides a high-performance anchor. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components to identify which matter most; if it underperforms, we learn that complexity is not the bottleneck and can pivot toward simpler or modality-specific designs. This is the highest-information-gain first experiment under a 10-run budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_020: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → acc 0.725), the most critical uncertainty is whether the RNA modality actually contributes meaningful signal over the image alone. Config_004 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer) is a direct ablation that holds the image encoder, aggregation, and profile setting constant while removing RNA. If image-only accuracy is close to 0.725, the multimodal fusion adds little and I should pivot budget toward optimizing the unimodal path; if it is substantially lower, multimodal fusion is confirmed as valuable and I can exploit that by tuning RNA encoder, fusion, and aggregation in subsequent runs. This single comparison resolves the highest-level design question and maximally informs the allocation of the remaining 8 experiments.

Evidence: config_020 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.725 accuracy, while image-only config_004 (imagenet_vit_l + transformer) collapses to 0.260, confirming the RNA modality is the primary signal carrier. This makes the RNA encoder choice the most impactful remaining uncertainty. Question: Does scgpt outperform scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder when paired with the same strong image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted) setup? Why this experiment: config_045 is a clean single-variable ablation (scgpt vs scvi_n200) on the best-performing backbone, directly testing whether a different RNA representation can push accuracy higher. With 7 experiments remaining, resolving this fundamental design choice early will inform whether to exploit the scgpt family or the scvi_n200 family for subsequent experiments, making it the highest-information next step.

Evidence: config_020 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) is the best at 0.725 acc, while config_045 (same but scgpt) drops to 0.520, confirming scvi_n200 is critical. config_004 (image_only) at 0.260 confirms multimodal fusion is essential. Uncertainty: we haven't tested whether the transformer aggregation is actually contributing or if a simpler avgpool suffices with the proven scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion pipeline. This experiment (config_010) isolates aggregation (avgpool vs transformer) while holding all other components at their best-known values. If avgpool matches or approaches 0.725, it tells us the transformer isn't adding value and we should redirect remaining budget to other levers (e.g., image encoder or profile setting). If transformer is clearly superior, it validates our architecture and we can focus on fine-tuning fusion or image encoder choices in the 6 remaining experiments.

The best result so far (config_020, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted fusion. The only untested variable within this exact top-performing architecture is the fusion method. config_039 is identical to config_020 except fusion=concat instead of weighted, providing a clean single-variable A/B test. This is the highest-value next experiment because: (1) it directly tests whether the current fusion strategy is optimal or a bottleneck, (2) if concat outperforms weighted, it opens a new optimization axis for the remaining 5 experiments, and (3) if weighted is confirmed superior, we can confidently fix fusion and pivot to exploring image encoder (resnet50) or profile setting in subsequent runs. With only 5 experiments left, reducing uncertainty on a variable within the known-best configuration is the most efficient use of the next slot.

Evidence: scvi_n200 consistently outperforms scgpt by ~0.20 accuracy (0.725 vs 0.520) in the same multimodal/multiprofile/transformer/weighted setup, confirming the RNA encoder is the most impactful variable. However, PCA_n2000 (a linear, high-dimensional projection) has not been tested in the best configuration. This experiment (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) isolates the RNA encoder choice while holding all other parameters at their best-known values. It will clarify whether the learned non-linear scvi representation is essential or whether a simpler high-dim linear projection suffices. This is the best use of experiment 6 because the RNA encoder is the largest source of performance variance observed, and resolving this question with 4 experiments remaining will guide whether to exploit scvi-based configs or explore alternative RNA representations in the final budget.

Evidence: config_020 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the clear best at 0.725 acc, with scvi_n200 strongly outperforming pca_n2000 (0.586) and scgpt (0.520), transformer beating avgpool (0.725 vs 0.706), and weighted ≈ concat (0.725 vs 0.721). The image encoder dimension is the only untested variable within this top-performing configuration space. Question: Does resnet50 as the image encoder complement scvi_n200 + transformer + weighted better than imagenet_vit_l, or does it underperform? Rationale: This is a clean single-variable swap from the current best, directly testing whether the ViT-L image features are truly optimal or if a CNN backbone could provide complementary information. With 3 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out the image encoder choice is critical before committing final budget to fine-tuning around the confirmed best architecture.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the dominant RNA encoder (0.725, 0.721, 0.713, 0.706 across configs), transformer is the best aggregation (0.725 vs 0.706 for avgpool), and the current best is config_020 (vit_l + weighted, acc 0.725). Notably, config_006 (resnet50 + weighted) achieved the highest F1 (0.6945) despite lower accuracy (0.713), suggesting resnet50 captures complementary discriminative information. We have tested vit_l+weighted (0.725), vit_l+concat (0.721), and resnet50+weighted (0.713), but the resnet50+concat combination remains untested. This experiment tests whether resnet50's stronger per-class discrimination (higher F1) synergizes with concat fusion to surpass the current best accuracy. With only 2 experiments remaining after this, exploiting the most promising untested combination in the proven multiprofile/scvi_n200/transformer subspace is the highest-value use of the next slot.

The current best (config_020: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.7250, and all tested multiprofile+transformer variants cluster tightly around 0.71-0.73. The key untested architectural question is whether the transformer aggregation step is truly necessary or whether a simpler singleprofile fusion (aggregation=None) with the same best encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) and weighted fusion could be competitive. Config_023 isolates this: it keeps the two strongest encoders and the best fusion strategy while removing the transformer, testing whether the added complexity of multiprofile+transformer is providing real signal or merely noise. Given only 1 experiment remains after this, this is the highest-information experiment: if singleprofile matches or exceeds 0.7250, it reveals a simpler, potentially more robust architecture; if it falls short, it confirms the transformer aggregation is a critical component and solidifies config_020 as the final answer. No other untested config combines the proven-best encoders with a structurally distinct architecture in a way that could plausibly surpass the current best.

The current best is config_020 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). Evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 as RNA encoder, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. Among remaining untested configs in this high-performing region, config_016 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted) is the closest logical extension: it retains the best RNA encoder and weighted fusion, and tests whether resnet50 (which showed competitive F1 of 0.6945 in config_006) combined with avgpool could produce a different inductive bias that might close or exceed the 0.7250 gap. Since this is the final experiment, it serves as the last exploitation attempt within the top-performing design subspace before confirming config_020 as the winner.
